cargo_toml_parse
#

cargo_toml.ts view source

cargo_toml_parse(contents: string): CargoMetadata

Extracts name/version/description/repository from the [package] and [workspace.package] tables of a Cargo.toml.

Deliberately not a full TOML parser: it scans for simple key = "value" string entries in those two tables, which covers both a single-crate manifest and a workspace root. Inline-table values like version = { workspace = true } (and the equivalent version.workspace = true) are ignored — a member crate inheriting from the workspace has no literal here, and fuz_repos only ever reads a repo's root manifest, where these are concrete. The first non-empty value for a key wins, so a top-level [package] takes precedence over [workspace.package] when both appear.

import {cargo_toml_parse} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/cargo_toml.js';

check_release_readiness

check_release_readiness(options: { report: { version: 21; workspace: string; registry: string; fetched: boolean; sessions: { kind: "available"; unscoped: { pid: number; cwd: string; worktree: string | null; process_cwd: string | null; source: "session_file" | "roster_worker"; }[]; } | { ...; }; entries: { ...; }[]; unregistered: ({ ...; } | ... 4 m... & RepoReadinessFormatOptions): ReleaseReadiness

Reads a repos status --fetch --json report for a release step: each key's entry ready (repo_readiness_for_publish), the report fetched, and busy detection available, since a live session it can't vouch for may be working in any checkout. A step commits rewrites in a dependent and names packages to publish, so a repo that isn't ready is held, and the reasons say how to fix it.

create_fs_fetch_value_cache
#

fs_fetch_value_cache.ts view source

create_fs_fetch_value_cache(name: string, dir?: string): Promise<FetchCache>

Creates file-system backed cache for fuz_util's fetch.js API responses.

Cache invalidation strategy: If cache file can't be read or parsed, entire cache is cleared (delete file) and starts fresh. This handles format changes.

Uses structuredClone to track changes - only writes to disk if data modified. Formatted with gro's format_file before writing for version control friendliness.

detect_cycles_by_type

(): { production_cycles: string[][]; dev_cycles: string[][]; }
#

Detects circular dependencies, categorized by severity.

Production/peer cycles prevent publishing (impossible to order packages). Dev cycles are normal (test utils, shared configs) and safely ignored.

Uses DFS traversal with recursion stack to identify back edges. Deduplicates cycles using sorted cycle keys.

returns object with production_cycles (errors) and dev_cycles (info)

fetch_repo_data
#

fetch_repo_data.ts view source

fetch_repo_data(options: FetchRepoDataOptions): Promise<RepoJson[]>

Fetches GitHub metadata (CI status, PRs) for all repos.

Fetches sequentially with a delay before each request to respect GitHub API rate limits. Uses await_in_loop intentionally to avoid parallel requests overwhelming the API. CI status is read for the branch each repo's registry entry follows (main when it names none), and that branch is written to RepoJson.branch.

A repo whose registry entry declares no CI (ci: false) isn't asked for check runs, and one with none on its branch isn't a failure: both leave check_runs null without logging. A failed fetch is logged as an error and leaves null for that repo's check_runs or pull_requests, and the remaining repos still fetch — except a 401 response or a repo URL without a GitHub owner, which throw.

import {fetch_repo_data} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/fetch_repo_data.js';

parameters

options

: FetchRepoDataOptions
#

the repos, credentials, cache, and pacing

returns

a RepoJson for each repo, in the order given

throws

  • Error - on a 401 response (check SECRET_GITHUB_API_TOKEN) or a repo whose URL has no GitHub owner

generate_publishing_plan
#

publishing_plan.ts view source

generate_publishing_plan(all_repos: LocalRepo[], options?: GeneratePlanOptions): Promise<PublishingPlan>

Generates the publishing plan in one pass over the prod/peer topological order. Each package's dependencies are settled before it is reached, so its required bump — from its prod/peer ranges against each dependency's version after the release — is final when computed: explicit changesets, escalation, or an auto-changeset, with no iteration.

Every package's version after the release is its predicted one when it publishes and its current one otherwise, so a dependent whose range trails a dependency's current version gets that rewrite too, along with the bump it implies.

import {generate_publishing_plan} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/publishing_plan.js';

options

?: GeneratePlanOptions = {}

group_into_levels
#

dependency_graph.ts view source

group_into_levels(order: readonly string[], get_dependencies: (name: string) => Iterable<string>, names?: ReadonlySet<string>, rank?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>): string[][]

Groups names into levels by their longest dependency path: a name's level is one past the deepest of its dependencies in names, and dependencies outside names don't count. So a level's names never depend on each other, and each depends only on names in earlier levels — work within a level can run in parallel. Within a level, names follow rank when given (config order, say), else order.

import {group_into_levels} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/dependency_graph.js';

parameters

order

: readonly string[]
#

every name to group, dependencies before dependents (a topological order)

get_dependencies

: (name: string) => Iterable<string>
#

the names one name depends on

names

?: ReadonlySet<string>
#

the names to group, a subset of order; defaults to all of it

rank

?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>
#

each name's position within its level; names it lacks go last

returns

the levels, shallowest first, with no empty level

needs_update
#

version_utils.ts view source

needs_update(current: string, new_version: string): boolean

Whether a dependency range must move to name new_version: a wildcard always does, and so does a range whose base version is older. One already naming it, or a newer version (a range staged ahead of a publish), doesn't — the rewrite never moves a range backward. A base that isn't x.y.z moves whenever it differs, and a protocol range (file:, workspace:, npm:) never.

import {needs_update} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/version_utils.js';

examples

needs_update('^0.54.0', '0.55.0') // true
needs_update('>=0.56.0', '0.55.0') // false

normalize_version_for_comparison(version: string): string

Normalizes version string for comparison.

Strips prefixes (^, ~, >=) to get bare version number. Handles wildcards as-is. Used by needs_update to compare versions.

examples

normalize_version_for_comparison('^1.2.3') // '1.2.3'

normalize_version_for_comparison('*') // '*'

predict_next_version(repo: LocalRepo, log?: Logger): Promise<{ version: string; bump_type: BumpType; } | null>

Predicts the next version by analyzing all changesets in a repo.

Reads all changesets, determines the highest bump type for the package, and calculates the next version. Returns null if no changesets found.

repo_readiness_for_gen
#

repo_readiness.ts view source

repo_readiness_for_gen(entry: ReposEntryStatus, options?: { allow_dirty?: boolean | undefined; }): { refused: RepoReadinessProblem[]; warned: RepoReadinessProblem[]; }

An entry's problems for gitops_sync, split by what they do to the run: refused stops it, warned is logged. Off its branch, dirty, or mid-operation refuses, since the site would show that working tree's modules beside origin's CI — unless allow_dirty, which reads the repo as it sits and warns instead. A checkout that can't be read, or an entry following no branch (only a reference follows none, and the config refuses references), always refuses. The followed branch not in sync with origin (behind, say: CI is origin's tip, the modules the local tree) and a failed fetch (the last fetch's view stands) warn. Busy sessions and needs_human reasons don't matter: generating writes nothing in the repo.

import {repo_readiness_for_gen} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/repo_readiness.js';

parameters

entry

: ReposEntryStatus
#

the entry as repos status --json reported it

options

?: { allow_dirty?: boolean | undefined; } = {}
#
  • options.allow_dirty — read a repo off its branch, dirty, or mid-operation as it sits

returns

the problems that refuse, and those that warn

repo_readiness_for_publish
#

repo_readiness.ts view source

repo_readiness_for_publish(entry: ReposEntryStatus): RepoReadinessProblem[]

The ways an entry isn't ready for a release step to rewrite or publish it: not at rest (repo_readiness_at_rest) other than its followed branch being ahead of origin, its fetch failed, another live session works in its primary checkout, or it has a needs_human reason. Ahead is ready: origin's tip is an ancestor of the branch, so the plan misses nothing and `gro publish`'s push stays a fast-forward, pushing those commits with the release. A reason restating an at-rest problem (the primary's operation or detached HEAD) is left out, and a default_branch_* reason stands in for the followed-branch problem it explains.

import {repo_readiness_for_publish} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/repo_readiness.js';

parameters

entry

: ReposEntryStatus
#

the entry as repos status --fetch --json reported it

returns

the problems; empty when the entry is ready

ReposOperations
#

operations.ts view source

Operations running the Rust repos binary, which owns fleet git state. Parsing its output is repos_status_load.ts's, not the runner's.

import type {ReposOperations} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/operations.js';

members

status

(options: { keys: string[]; registry?: string | undefined; fetch?: boolean | undefined; }): Promise<Result>
#

Runs repos [--registry <path>] status [--fetch] <keys…> --json in the process's cwd and returns what it printed, whatever its exit code. With fetch, repos fetches each entry from origin first, which writes remote-tracking refs and nothing else. Fails only when the binary didn't run to an exit: not_found when it isn't on PATH.

required_bump_for_dependency_update
#

version_utils.ts view source

required_bump_for_dependency_update(current_version: string, has_breaking_deps: boolean): BumpType

The bump a package must take when one of its prod/peer dependencies updates. Pre-1.0: minor for a breaking dependency, otherwise patch. 1.0+: major for a breaking dependency, otherwise patch.

Single source of truth for the dependency-driven bump rule, shared by the plan (generate_publishing_plan) and the auto-changeset generator (calculate_required_bump) so the two never drift.

route_human_output
#

output_helpers.ts view source

route_human_output(log: Logger, machine: boolean): WriteStdout

Keeps a task's stdout for its machine-readable document or stream when machine is set: the logger's info and debug lines, which it writes with console.log, go where its errors go — stderr — and child loggers inherit that. Gro hands a task the logger its own lines go through, so gro's lines after the task runs (✓, the timings) follow to stderr; the two it prints before the task runs (invoking, → <task>) stay on stdout, out of the task's reach.

import {route_human_output} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/output_helpers.js';

to_dependency_updates
#

publishing_plan_helpers.ts view source

to_dependency_updates(repo: LocalRepo, targets: ReadonlyMap<string, string>, changes: ReadonlyMap<string, VersionChange>, sections?: readonly DependencySection[]): DependencyUpdate[]

The updates one package's dependency ranges need so each names its dependency's version after the release: targets maps every package to that version, its predicted one when it publishes and its current one otherwise. A range already naming it, or staged ahead of it, needs none (needs_update).

An update is breaking when the move from the range's base version is (to_range_update_bump), so a range lagging its dependency's last release counts what it skips; a range with no x.y.z base takes the dependency's own change's breaking flag.

update_package_json
#

dependency_updater.ts view source

update_package_json(repo: LocalRepo, updates: readonly DependencyUpdate[], options?: UpdatePackageJsonOptions): Promise<void>

Rewrites one dependent's package.json for its dependency updates and commits it, with its auto-changeset when it republishes.

Workflow:

  1. Rewrites each updated name in every section that lists it (dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies), so a package that is both a peer and a dev dependency moves in one commit
  2. Writes updated package.json in the indentation it was read with, so the rewrite moves only the ranges (npm also takes its lockfile's indentation from it)
  3. With changeset, writes the dependent's one auto-changeset for its prod/peer updates, merging into it when an earlier rewrite wrote it (write_dependency_updates_changeset)
  4. Commits both package.json and changeset, the message naming each updated version

Each range keeps its existing prefix, else takes the strategy's (to_updated_range). When no entry's value changes — every range already names its version — it writes, creates, and commits nothing, or throws under changeset.

import {update_package_json} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/dependency_updater.js';

parameters

repo

: LocalRepo
#

the dependent

updates

: readonly DependencyUpdate[]
#

its dependency updates, all naming repo as the dependent

options

?: UpdatePackageJsonOptions = {}
#

throws

  • Error - if file operations or git operations fail, or if nothing changes for a republishing dependent (changeset), whose changeset would go missing

type "explicit" | "escalation" | "auto"

How a version change arises in the plan: from the package's own changesets (explicit), from its changesets with the bump raised to what a breaking dependency requires (escalation), or from a changeset generated for a dependency update (auto).

wait_for_package
#

npm_registry.ts view source

wait_for_package(pkg: string, version: string, options: WaitOptions, deps: NpmRegistryDeps): Promise<void>

Waits for package version to propagate to NPM registry.

Uses exponential backoff with jitter to avoid hammering registry. Logs progress every 5 attempts. Respects timeout to avoid infinite waits.

Critical for multi-repo publishing: ensures published packages are available before updating dependent packages.

import {wait_for_package} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/npm_registry.js';

parameters

options

: WaitOptions
#
  • options.max_attempts — max poll attempts (default 30)
  • options.initial_delay — starting delay in ms (default 1000)
  • options.max_delay — max delay between attempts (default 60000)
  • options.timeout — total timeout in ms (default 300000 = 5min)

throws

  • Error - if timeout reached or max attempts exceeded

write_dependency_updates_changeset
#

changeset_generator.ts view source

write_dependency_updates_changeset(repo: LocalRepo, updates: DependencyVersionChange[], options?: { log?: Logger | undefined; fs_ops?: FsOperations | undefined; }): Promise<string>

Writes the dependent's auto-generated changeset, merging updates into the one it already has: an earlier step of the release wrote it when another dependency was rewritten. A dependency listed in both keeps its earliest from_version and takes the latest to_version; the bump is recomputed over the merged list, never below the file's own.

import {write_dependency_updates_changeset} from '@fuzdev/fuz_repos/changeset_generator.js';
